title: Control plane: persist RolloutPlan/Stage/Gate with versioned schema migrations
creator: Ethan Park
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Implement first-class persistence for Dedicated staged rollouts in the control plane.

Context
Dedicated pools currently do “all-at-once” changes at the pool level and lack safe staged rollout primitives. This ticket adds the persistent control-plane objects that everything else (APIs, routing/policy evaluation, gate evaluator, console) depends on.

Scope
- Define control-plane storage model for RolloutPlan, Stage, Gate, EvaluationWindow, and state/audit references.
- Implement versioned schema migrations (forward-only) with a clear upgrade story and backwards compatibility for readers during rollout.
- Add validation rules and invariants at write time (and in DB constraints where possible).
- Ensure idempotent creation semantics and safe concurrent updates (optimistic concurrency) for plan updates.

Data model (high-level)
- rollout_plans
  - id (uuid)
  - tenant_id
  - pool_id
  - target (model_version/runtime_config hash reference)
  - spec_json (canonical normalized spec)
  - status (draft|active|paused|aborted|completed)
  - plan_version (int, monotonic)
  - created_by / updated_by (actor id)
  - created_at / updated_at
- rollout_plan_stages
  - id (uuid)
  - rollout_plan_id
  - stage_index (int)
  - name
  - traffic_weight_bps (int, 0–10000)
  - requires_approval (bool)
  - evaluation_window_seconds (int)
  - min_duration_seconds (int, optional)
- rollout_stage_gates
  - id (uuid)
  - rollout_stage_id
  - gate_type (latency_p95|error_5xx|timeouts|gpu_util|queue_depth|custom)
  - comparator (<=, <, >=, >)
  - threshold (stringified numeric)
  - query_ref (string; points to query template + params)
  - missing_data_policy (hold|fail|skip) [v1 default: hold]

Invariants / validation (v1)
- Only one active RolloutPlan per (tenant_id, pool_id).
- Stage weights must be strictly increasing and end at 100% (10000 bps).
- Stage 0 is allowed to be 0% (shadow/internal), but must have explicit gates if it can advance automatically.
- Gate types are limited to the beta-required set; unknown/custom gate types rejected until evaluator supports them.
- Missing metrics must not auto-advance; missing_data_policy defaults to HOLD.
- Updates require matching plan_version (optimistic concurrency). If mismatch, return conflict.

Migration strategy
- Add tables in a new migration, no writes at first.
- Ship dual-read capability behind a feature flag for internal dogfood environments (Dedicated only).
- Backfill is not required (new feature). Ensure clean drop/rollback procedure is documented for staging only.

Acceptance criteria
- Migrations apply cleanly in dev/staging/prod (tested with the release pipeline).
- Create/update of RolloutPlan is idempotent (client-supplied idempotency key supported by API layer later; for this ticket ensure DB can tolerate retries and unique constraints are correct).
- Concurrency-safe updates using plan_version.
- Unit tests for validation + basic persistence operations.
- Documentation note for schema versioning + how to add new gate types safely.

Non-goals
- API endpoints (ENG-5122).
- Gate evaluation engine (ENG-5124).
- Audit event export (ENG-5128).
comments: 2025-01-08 (Ethan Park): Please align IDs/foreign keys with existing control-plane conventions (uuid v4, created_at/updated_at triggers). Also, avoid storing “live state” in spec tables; status/state machine should live at plan level with separate event log.

2025-01-10 (Michael Nguyen): For plan_version, use int with default 1 and increment on any spec mutation. Readers should treat spec_json as immutable per version; if we need historical versions later we can add rollout_plan_versions without rewriting everything.

2025-01-14 (Benji Okafor): Draft schema proposal: 3 tables (plans, stages, gates) + JSON spec column for canonical spec. Added unique index on (tenant_id, pool_id) WHERE status IN ('draft','active','paused') to prevent multiple concurrent plans. Question: should ‘aborted’ plans remain queryable by pool? (leaning yes; soft-retain for audit).

2025-01-16 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): RBAC isn’t in scope here, but please make sure actor fields can store both internal operators and enterprise users (principal_id + principal_type). We’ll wire auth later, but schema shouldn’t assume only internal actors.

2025-01-21 (Jordan Lee): Routing needs stable stage IDs even if stage names change. Please generate stage UUIDs at creation and never regenerate on updates; avoid using stage_index as identifier in downstream configs.

2025-01-23 (Benji Okafor): Implemented validation for monotonic weights + terminal 100%. Added CHECK constraints for bps range and stage_index >= 0. Left “strictly increasing” as application-level validation (DB constraint not feasible across rows).
2025-01-27 (Ethan Park): Please ensure we can do a safe “update plan spec while paused” flow (plan_version increments, status remains paused). Console will rely on this to edit without resuming.
2025-02-03 (Benji Okafor): Added paused edit support + version bump. Added ‘spec_hash’ for quick equality check and to detect no-op updates. Also added migration notes on forward-only behavior.

2025-02-10 (Leila Farouk): Verified migrations apply in staging and that create->update conflict path returns expected error. Flagged one issue: stage weights accept [0,10000] but validation didn’t reject duplicate values; fixed in latest patch.

2025-02-12 (Ethan Park): Marking done. API work (ENG-5122) can now depend on the persistence layer; please coordinate with Chloe on the model serialization format (spec_json canonicalization) to avoid churn.
